content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To find the range of a data set, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Write down the final range value on the report (1 minute)
Step 2. Clean the raw data of any non-numeric symbols (1 hour)
Step 3. Identify the smallest value in the sorted list (5 minutes)
Step 4. Double-check the math for the range calculation (10 minutes)
Step 5. Upload the dataset to the cloud server (20 minutes)
Step 6. Locate the physical ledger containing the data (30 minutes)
Step 7. Sharpen pencils for manual tallying (2 minutes)
Step 8. Scan the list for the absolute maximum value (15 minutes)
Step 9. Sort the data in ascending order (45 minutes)
Step 10. Verify that no data points were skipped (12 minutes)
Step 11. Highlight the outliers in the dataset (5 minutes)
Step 12. Cross-reference the data with the original source (2 hours)
Step 13. Run a script to find the minimum value (3 minutes)
Step 14. Check the data for duplicate entries (25 minutes)
Step 15. Create a backup of the digital file (10 minutes)
Step 16. Print a summary of the statistical findings (8 minutes)
Step 17. Save the final spreadsheet (1 minute)
Step 18. Ask a colleague to review the data entry (30 minutes)
Step 19. Identify the data type of each column (15 minutes)
Step 20. Clear the workspace of distractions (5 minutes)
Step 21. Open the statistical software (2 minutes)
Step 22. Download the raw data file (10 minutes)
Step 23. Import the data into the workspace (5 minutes)
Step 24. Label the columns of the data set (10 minutes)
Step 25. Check for missing values in the rows (40 minutes)
Step 26. Subtract the minimum value from the maximum value (2 minutes)
Step 27. Run a descriptive statistics command (1 minute)
Step 28. Manually transcribe the data from the ledger (3 hours)
Step 29. Compare the calculated maximum against the data set (10 minutes)
Step 30. Organize the data into a structured table (50 minutes)
Step 31. Perform a final audit of the sorted data (20 minutes)
Step 32. Calibrate the calculator (30 seconds)
Step 33. Set up the project folder (15 minutes)
Step 34. Turn on the computer (3 minutes)
Step 35. Review the distribution of the data (25 minutes)
Step 36. Clear the calculator memory (10 seconds)
Step 37. Format the data table for the final report (15 minutes)
Step 38. Document the range calculation method (15 minutes)
Step 39. Email the data summary to the supervisor (5 minutes)
Step 40. Log into the secure data portal (2 minutes)
Step 41. Verify the page numbers of the ledger (5 minutes)
Step 42. Verify the minimum value against the raw data (10 minutes)
Step 43. Note the spread of the data (5 minutes)
Step 44. Validate the integrity of the data points (1 hour)
Step 45. Check the internet connection (1 minute)
Step 46. Filter out irrelevant data categories (20 minutes)
Step 47. Confirm the maximum value is correct (5 minutes)
Step 48. Sign the data verification form (2 minutes)
Step 49. Draft the conclusion section (40 minutes)
Step 50. Archive the project notes (15 minutes)
